content.title: Japan stocks soar after Takaichi elected as ruling party leader
content.summary:
STORY: Japanese stocks soared Monday after Sanae Takaichi came out on top to lead Japan's ruling party.

That makes her set to become the country's first female prime minister, subject to confirmation by lawmakers.  

The Nikkei surged close to 5% to hit a new record high.

It passed the 48,000-mark for the first time, as analysts broadly welcomed her commitment to economic stimulus. 

Defense contractor Mitsubishi Heavy Industries was among the top movers, jumping around 11% as more military spending is expected under Takaichi.

Tech stocks also surged, with chip gear maker Advantest jumping 14%. 

:: October 4, 2025

The veteran lawmaker won Saturday's run-off vote in the Liberal Democratic Party race.

Upon victory, Takaichi made clear her priority would be to revive demand and the broader market. 

Known to be an advocate of big fiscal spending, she is a devotee of the stimulus policies developed by her late predecessor Shinzo Abe. 

Takaichi has called for tax cuts to cushion the rising cost of living.

And she's criticized the Bank of Japan's decision to raise interest rates, dimming bets rates will be hiked at its meeting at the end of October.

That saw the yen sink, trading at 150 yen against the dollar.

Longer-term Japanese government bonds also fell, on the expectations Takaichi will push for more spending.
